name: Quobly
description: Quobly develops silicon spin qubit quantum computers leveraging semiconductor manufacturing techniques. Based in Grenoble near CEA-Leti, the company focuses on building scalable quantum processors using established silicon fabrication processes.
funding: EUR 134M+ (seed EUR 19M; Series A EUR 115M, June 2026)

news.title: Quobly raises €115M Series A to commercialise silicon-based quantum computers
news.excerpt: The round was led by Bpifrance and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council (EIC Fund), ALIAD (Air Liquide Venture Capital), Blast, and existing investor Innovacom. Quobly plans to launch its Alloy Pioneer system via cloud in 2026.

news.title: Quantum startup Quobly raises €115m backed by STMicroelectronics
news.excerpt: Quobly, the French startup building quantum computers, has raised a €115m Series A to move the production of its technology from lab to industrial scale.

news.title: Quobly secures €115M Series A
news.excerpt: A milestone toward commercial silicon quantum computers. Series A led by Bpifrance, STMicroelectronics and SEALSQ, with participation from leading industrial and deeptech investors, to accelerate the industrialization of quantum processors.

news.title: Quobly and SEALSQ Sign $5M Commercial Agreement to Embed Post-Quantum Security in Silicon Quantum Computers
news.excerpt: Quobly and SEALSQ Corp (Nasdaq: LAES) signed a $5M commercial agreement to integrate SEALSQ's post-quantum cryptography and hardware Root-of-Trust infrastructure into Quobly's silicon spin-qubit systems, including the Alloy Pioneer system targeted for cloud access by end of 2026.

news.title: Quobly Demonstrates Single-Chip Readout and Gates on 300 mm Industrial Silicon Process
news.excerpt: Quobly achieved single-chip execution of qubit readout, single-qubit gates, and two-qubit gates on its QSOI® architecture fabricated at STMicroelectronics' commercial 300 mm FD-SOI production line in Crolles, France, validating its approach to manufacturing silicon quantum processors at industrial scale.

news.title: Quobly and CEA-Leti Strengthen Collaboration via FAMES Pilot Line to Scale 300 mm Silicon Spin-Qubit Platform
news.excerpt: Quobly expanded its joint technology programme with CEA-Leti by securing direct access to the European FAMES Pilot Line, providing tools to prototype 3D integration, RF control layers, and process flows for next-generation silicon spin-qubit processors.
